newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent steadies after July gas oil expiry.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent steadies after July gas oil expiry.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were steadier at lower levels after gyrations in gas oil futures ahead of the IPE July contract's expiry today which dragged crude down through technical support levels, brokers said.

August Brent was 16 cents a barrel lower at 1205 GMT and was trading at $18.06. The July gas oil contract ended $1.25 a tonne down on the day at $161.25 and August, the new front month, was also $1.25 weaker at $162.00.
"There has been a bit of fund selling," one broker said, adding that there was little in the way of fresh fundamental news behind the falls.
Brent fell back through support levels at around $18.08 a barrel and reached as low as $17.92 at one point. But volumes were thin.
Dealers were awaiting fresh news about when Iraq oil exports under the country's oil-fo-food deal with the U.N. were likely to resume.
Technical analysts said they saw a variety of support levels down to $17.32 a barrel, the front-month low reached on June 11.
